What are things you accidentally did because of the sheer exhaustion of having a newborn? I'll go first, my wife and I are first time parents to a beautiful two month old little boy. Anyway just like many parents who have newborns, we are utterly exhausted. After a particularly rough night with the baby, I was doing laundry the next morning and somehow my wife's switch ended up in the laundry basket. I didn't notice it, I just stupidly dumped everything in the washer and only noticed it later when I was taking out the clothes. 

Tried everything but it's dead, my wife was so devastated that she cried. I have apologized and she says it's ok but I haven't stopped feeling horrible ever since it's happened. Mind you, the switch was relatively new , we bought it after our child was born and it was really helping her mentally with being post partum and all. Hopefully one day we can look back and laugh about it. Please tell me your stories to make me feel better. 


 Was buying something from Facebook Marketplace that was $50 cash. The day before I went, I checked my wallet and had $40. I went to our safe and got $5 from our stash so I’d have the needed $50. Day of, checked my wallet to be sure I had $50 - saw two twenties and one five, so knew I had what I needed. Drove 30 mins to the persons house, grabbed my money from my wallet (again checking that it’s $50), picked up the item from the owner and said “$50, right?”. Handed over the $50. As I’m putting the item in my trunk they come up and tell me I’d only given them $45. Only then did it click that $40+$5 is $45, not $50. Went 24 hours thinking it was. Luckily I was buying a nursery item so the person completely understood the fatigue I was/am experiencing and didn’t think I was trying to rip them off.

She loves band shirts (though her tastes are very metal), flames, dragons, spikes, basically her room looks like Bowser's lair. Problem is, she's not even close to adult sizes (she's in a size 8 for an oversized fit), and I don't know where to find goth girl/metalhead couture in kids medium. Hot topic???? Jealous of my time I had kids late at 42 and 44. Have a 4 and a 3 year old now. It's been half a decade (since pregnancy) and I don't know if it's possible to love my children and dislike having children...

I always worked a lot in a demanding career and used my off work time to decompress, mostly by working out and reading. 

I feel that now I have little time to decompress between the end of the workday and being with them after daycare. I also have senior dogs I have to walk 60-90 min a day, so instead of working out I am giving my dogs somw attention in their final years. 

Then I get resentful because the girls go to bed between 8:30 and 9:30 - always waking up and whining for another 60 min afterwards. And, after reading them books in bed I get mellow and completely useless. 

I am so resentful. I wonder if it feels "better" when they just stop demanding your attention so much. I get angry when they call me or cry at night for no reason. This is not a good feeling to have. 

Am I just not meant for this?

PS: we have a nanny, great daycare, and my husband is a fantastic stay at home dad. He takes care of their every meal , housework. I take care of finances, their health appointments and management, clothes/shoes shopping, and also purchase most books. Still, they call me whining and cry, throwing themselves at my feet, as if I was abandoning them, if I even try to cook in their presence instead of dedicating my full attention to them. I usually spend 3-5 hours taking care of them daily, plus full weekends. I feel very worn out. I just want to live without all this pressure every single day. I can't even go to the toilet without a child crying at the door. 

UPDATE: 

I love your guys responses, tips, care. I feel so looked after. Thank you!!! May God bless you!

For extra context: 

- I am a recovering workaholic with mild autism (aspergers), have hyperfocus and a lot of trouble with the toddlers noise - super high pitched yelling, overall speaking super loudly - and scattered minds.

- my husband does the all the everyday food ahopping and cooking, I only do it to decompress (and because my cooking repertoire is better ha), he does an insane amount of laundry, cleaning after our pooping/peeing Alzheimers dogs, picks up the girls, brings them to the park and extracurriculars. Our older child is special needs (ARFID) and has been on and off the hospital for most of her life until I dragged everyone to Europe to get proper chronic illness healthcare (it's working!!!), which increases the workload but also the need for an available parent to hold on when she is at home sick.  I would hire a dog walker. That way your dogs are happy when they get home. You can spend time with your kids with that extra time. And maybe they will be a little less clingy by dinner and bedtime, cause they got some time with you? An idea

When does it get easier? I’m exhausted. I know this question sounds dumb and I know that every age has their challenges. But I’m really feeling defeated this morning and I’m very much questioning having a second child (always wanted two, but now that I have one I’m not sure anymore). 

My daughter is 17 months old. I didn’t find the baby phase that difficult. Sure, didn’t get much sleep, but at least she was stationary and napped multiple times a day. My now 17 months old is so difficult, and that’s probably very normal. Instead of playing with her toys, her favorite thing to do is trying to pull everything off the shelves, climbing furniture, screaming at doors that are closed, taking away my coffee mug with hot coffee (I don’t let her and then it’s screaming again), throwing food and water on the floor etc etc. she throws tantrums all the time, and never listens. Constantly tries to run away wherever we are (she’s damn fast at this point), goes up to strangers at the playground and demands their snacks (no matter how many snacks I bring), tries to steal other kids toys and stuff from unattended strollers, etc etc. She can never sit still and hates diaper changes and me trying to put clothes on her. 

I’m so tired and mentally exhausted, feeling constantly anxious, my favorite time of the day is when she’s at daycare or asleep. I’m sad I feel this way and I’m very much questioning having a second child (I don’t have years and years to decide because I’m 37 already). 

Parents of older children (or even older toddlers) - WHEN does it get easier? Please tell me I’m not gonna feel like this for the next years to come. Please tell me that once she’s more verbal it won’t be as freaking exhausting and frustrating to be a parent. I’m so overstimulated and anxious all the time. I love my daughter and we do have fun too, but I can absolutely not say that this is my favorite age so far.  It’s so difficult, I’m going through the same thing. It really helps to know I’m not alone, so thank you! Trouble is, when they’re babies we’re told to respond every time they’re upset! Always do exactly what they want. And now I get confused, what behaviours do I respond to, and how? If she’s having a tantrum that she can’t pull the cats tail, do I soothe her? Do I say no firmly? Do I ignore her completely? Such a battle! And then I’m always questioning if I’m doing the right thing, if I’m a bad mum.

My 5 year old is mean. I know we’re not supposed to compare our kids but the older my toddler gets the more I realize my son is kinda mean and I don’t know what to do about it. 

My son is 5. He’s very polite when we’re out in public. He plays well with other kids and does sports.  He’s very outgoing and is comfortable talking to adults and children and asking people to be his friend. He’s always getting complimented by older people about how nice and polite my kids are. He can be a little loud and wild but most of the time he’s very nice. 

When it comes to at home though he’s totally lazy and refuses to do anything for himself, he’s selfish and mean to his sister. He’s constantly got an attitude. For example if we’re on a walk and his sister falls and scrapes her knee and cries he will completely walk over her to tell me he saw a squirrel. If she wants to play with him he tells her no but will then complain he doesn’t have anyone to play with. If I tell him to clean his room (which he’s totally capable of doing and mostly involves picking up his toys and straightening his bed) he will throw a fit. He’ll complain that he’s too tired to do anything anyone asks him to do He’ll volunteer to help me cook and then get bored and walk away 5 minutes in. If he’s hungry and I don’t feed him immediately he gets hangry and complains and whines until he’s fed. Meanwhile if he watches a movie and it’s just kinda sad he’ll sob like his heart is broken but his sister or I could be seriously hurt or sick and he doesn’t care at all. 

I’ve never just let him do whatever we wanted either. He’s had a chore chart since he was 3 and he as very good at doing his chores. Now it’s been basically abandoned. He used to help me do laundry and fold clothes, he was into helping with dishes and cooking. I got him a swiffer so he could mop with me and he doesn’t even bother. The only time he wants to help is if my daughter is helping and he feels left out. As of right now he’s fully responsible for cleaning up the playroom and his bedroom along with school work. 

Now my daughter on the other hand is constantly thinking of her brother. She’s 2 and if he’s hurt she’s comforting him. If he’s upset she’s talking him through it and telling him to breathe. She’ll hug him if he’s sad. She even feeds him food off of her own plate if he says he’s still hungry. We’ve given her the same lessons on caring for others. It makes me wonder if I’ve done something wrong or if this is just normal. Maybe it’s a boy girl thing? 


Edit: I wanted to add that his meanness comes out more toward me and his father. For example he wanted me to play a song from a group called Baby Beard and I tried putting it on the Alexa but it wasn’t playing so I recommended he listen to Babymetal because they’re a similar group and I played the song for him and within a few seconds he started saying “wow mom you really want me to listen to this? This song is dumb. You really think this is good?” And I was so flabbergasted I said “if you’re going to be disrespectful when I try to show you something then we don’t have to do it you can go listen to music in your room”. He has the same attitude with my husband about anything and everything. He’s not always mean like this but it’s common enough that it’s concerning.  My 5 yo is the same, I never thought of it as mean. This is normal for kid her age. Of course she won’t cook with me, it is boring activity even for me.

Phone Limits Child is 11. Im her foster parent.  Will be 12 in December. She has had some trauma and never had screen limitations prior to living with us. Her mom and dad are drug addicts. She has lived with us for a year now. We have limits for screen time and downtime for her phone. Screen time is 3 hours a day. Downtime is from 10pm to 7am. She has access to music 24/7. We give her breaks from screentime and downtime on school breaks. Last night she sent us multiple texts requesting that she not have a time limit anymore. I texted her back saying that this was something that we would have discuss and that it was not happening last night. My husband asked her why it is a big deal all of the sudden and she responded with basically I dont want limits anymore. I make good grades, I do my chores, I get up on time, I dont stay up late, and im tired a being put in a crib. She decided that she did not like our answer and proceeded to destroy all the birthday cards/holiday cards I got for her and decided that she was going to pull all of her clothes out of her closet. I calmed her down and went to bed. Woke up to a letter with her saying that she wants no limits because she wants to he able to communicate with her friend later than usual. He is a 13 year old boy. I'm at my whits end with this. Several of her friends have no limitations. Are we doing too much?  It sounds like the sudden change is for a boyfriend.  Devices off by 10:00pm? Entirely reasonable.  Kids should be sleeping.  I have similar limits for my 11 FS.  If I didn't, he would be on devices 24/7, which is unhealthy.  I always frame things by what is healthy and reasonable, and I think it's okay to say "It doesn't matter what your friends are doing.  You have healthy limits" and stick with what you think is best.  Tell her to let her friends/boyfriend know when she is using her device, and they can talk then.  Healthy limit.  My kid has \~2 hours/weekday with devices off by 8:30.  He gets a lot more time on weekends, but there is time that we have devices off and away on weekends too, and it never interrupts things we already have planned.  He has to put his devices away in the kitchen at night, and I always check that they're there.  No one needs to be texting in the middle of the night.  Teens need enough sleep to function and be at their best for school and just in general as they are growing.  I feel bad for the kids who have no limits.  Those who DO have limits may realize when they are adults that the limits were helpful even though right now it doesn't seem that way.

Just. Clean. Your. Room. My daughter recently turned 13 and her room is just constantly a disaster. I know that some of that just comes with age, but this is beyond livable. It’s not just clothes not put away, we’re talking dirty tissues and makeup pads and q-tips all over the floor, scraps of paper and fabric from craft projects littered all over, layers of stuff on the floor so that there is no usable path through, etc. Things break or are lost frequently. And she has zero respect for the value of items or desires to take care of her things. 

I feel like we’ve done it all. From me cleaning her room entirely, multiple times, hauling away bags of trash in the hopes that it would help her keep it clean if she’s starting from a clean slate…donating tons of clothes and things to make it easier to visually see where things go…bringing in extra storage to put things in…

I’ve yelled. I’ve pleaded. I’ve taken away privileges and electronics. Assigned dollar values to different chores to reward her for doing them. Not let her go do things unless her room was cleaned. I’ve written task lists, told her to write her own lists…I’m out of ideas. She is perfectly content to just live in rot, and it’s starting to spill into other areas of the house too.

I stayed home from work today and cleaned it again, and found ants in her room. This is actually the second time that’s happened in the past 6 months. There’s a difference between messy and filthy, and it’s filthy. Something has to change. But how do I make that happen?  Soooo what worked for my dad when I was living in a pig sty was to tell me I wasn't allowed *in* my room til it was clean. I could go in there to clean, get clothes, or sleep. Period. I had to change in the bathroom. I wasn't allowed to keep a light on when I went in to sleep. All cleaning had to happen with the door open so he could see i was actively cleaning. 

Im sure it was absolute fucking torture for him, too, because I'm sure I made life miserable whining for a week. 

But it worked. I cleaned it up and never let it get truly out of hand again.

Should I talk to someone about the security officer at my child’s school? Hey, all. I’m a single father to a nine-year-old girl. None of my other friends have children, and I need advice. I’m feeling very defensive and am wondering if I need to talk to the school about something that happened recently.

My child came home from school today and told me the security officer had made a comment about her outfit. She was wearing a dress that was age-appropriate and just above her ankles in length. She states she was in line for lunch, and the security officer said to her, “Do I need to call your dad to ask him to get you some pants?”

I’m confused why he said this. I’ve been asking my child questions to try to learn more, but the whole thing seems bizarre to me. I’ll list some other bits of information that might answer some immediate questions:

- She does not wear skirts or dresses every day or even most days. She wears pants and shorts. The temperatures have been in the 90°s.

- There were no other grown ups around when he said this to her (which is sort of a red flag to me).

- She felt “a little embarrassed.” When he said it, but she is as puzzled as I am as to why he said it.

- We have never had any problems in the three years we’ve been at this school.

- She does not and has never come to school in clothes which would violate the dress code.


***
So my question is this: What do I do? 
I feel the need to go to the school, but my fear is that I won’t be taken seriously or will be seen as some overbearing or overly defensive father no matter how neutrally I approach the situation.
Ultimately, I’m not saying I want the guy fired or that I’m expecting an apology even. I genuinely want to understand why he said that, but the bottom line is that I don’t feel that was appropriate, and I want that known. I don’t feel it’s appropriate for a grown man to tease a little girl (who he has power over) about what she’s wearing. I want the security officer to know that *I know* what he said to her. I want him to know that my child tells me when she feels uncomfortable. Is there a way I can navigate this situation without making things worse while also ensuring I’ve done my job to protect her?
 If you feel comfortable with the administration, tell the principal. It definitely should be addressed in a way like “hey, daughter said that a happened and it made her confused and uncomfortable because of b. I am not 100% sure of all the facts so I am wanting to discuss the incident with you so we can solve this together.” Something along those lines. If anything you can also reach out to her teacher.

If they are a good administration they will take you seriously. If they don’t or you are unhappy with the way they handle it, you could reach out to the school board. Also, keep documentation on this in case it’s the beginning of something. And you never know if this officer has had people complain about him in the past either so it should definitely get spoken about.

Slowly dying inside I feel like I’m doomed to become a bitter old lady. I constantly talk to my kids and my husband about how I need their help cleaning up, or at the very least just not making more messes, but I just feel like they can’t be bothered.

I’m constantly brain storming ways to make things easier for everyone. I ask why certain tasks and chores are hard to complete and then I change the way they are done.

My kids said their chores were unfair so we had a family meeting and sat down and agreed what would be fair, very little change. My husband leaves all is laundry in the corner of our bathroom despite having a hamper on his side of the bed so I added a hamper in the bathroom. Clothes still on the floor. He doesn’t do his laundry on his side so it’s constantly over flowing (I do everyone else’s, mine plus 4 kids and the household laundry). He says he’s too tired and we should just switch sides of the bed so I don’t see it when I walk in the room. 

The shoes are always a mess in the entry so I bought more shoe racks and organized all the shoes to show they would fit. Shoes on the floor still. 

I’m trying my best to do as much as I can on my own, ask for help when I need it, have reasonable expectations, solve problems, but it just really feels like no one cares until I’m wildly depressed or having a breakdown. 

If I do every break down and cry or have a fit things will get better for a bit, but it’s pretty much right back to nothingness right after. 

I feel like the support character in my own life, and I can feel myself growing resentful of my husband and kids. I’m afraid it will be too late by the time anyone in my house decides to change in a meaningful way, but I don’t know what else do to advocate for myself. I think you’re going about this the wrong way. Instead of trying to make everything easier, make it more annoying and inconvenient.

An important fact is that you don’t need your family‘s help to clean up. They need to clean up after themselves and do their chores, because they live in a shared home. It is their own responsibility. Taking care of your own responsibilities and helping someone else with theirs are two entirely different things.

Bedroom isn’t the right place for dirty laundry. I would take that hamper out of the bedroom and put it next to the other hampers. I would tell my husband, that any dirty laudry lying on the bedroom floor at the end of the day, will go straight in a plastic bag and on the driver’s seat of his car or to some other place where it will not bother you but will inconvenience him. If he removes it from there and puts it anywhere else but in thehamper or the washing machine, you’ll treat it as rubish and throw it in the bin. Dirty laudry lying on the bathroom floor right next to the hamper would go straight into a plastic bag and in the bin. There is no excuse for that, unless you came back from a long trip with a huge amount of laundry, someone got sick or something similar.

Shoes in the hallway? Tell everyone, you will put all the shoes lying on the floor in plastic bags and leave them on their beds. They will soon learn that it is a lot easier to take the shoes from the shoe rack in the hallway than having to go all the way to their bedroom to get them.

Don’t get depressed and don’t get angry about the mess, just make sure you make it your family’s problem in a such a way that it causes them extra work and inconvenience end gets the mess out of your sight.

If you write more examples of chores that are often left undone, we can help come up with ideas on how to make the issue your family’s problem instead of yours.

Good luck!

Do y’all send your kids to daycare in stained clothes? I was doing laundry, and found my son’s (3yo) favorite Bluey shirt. It’s stained around the neckline with spots of spaghetti sauce. I don’t want people to think we’re dirty, neglectful, or can’t provide for our kids.  Occasional stained shirt on a 3yo?  Nobody is going to think twice.

Stained shirt most days?  You might get judged but you're still not doing anything wrong. 🤣

How are we getting our pre-teen boys up and out the door on time for school? EDIT: We had a chat after school yesterday and I let him know that he is old enough to start taking responsibility for himself in the mornings. I told him that I will no longer be nagging him to get up - I will come in once to wake him up and the rest is up to him. If he’s not downstairs and ready to go by 7:35, no electronics for the day. Guess who was ready to go on time this morning? I did give him a 5 minute warning but that’s it. This was only day 1 so we’ll see how it goes moving forward, but it was much smoother. Thanks for all of the advice and opinions. As a single mom with zero involvement from my ex, sometimes it’s hard to tell if I’m being too harsh or too lenient so I appreciate the outside perspectives.

Son is 12. Also have an 8 year old daughter. I’ll start this by saying none of us are morning people. However we are running late to school nearly every day because he doesn’t want to get out of bed. 

We take care of most things the night before - shower, laying out clothes for the next day (my daughter even wears her clothes to bed so it’s one less thing to do in the morning), getting backpacks together, etc - and they eat breakfast at school, so all he really has to do in the morning is put clothes on and brush his teeth. We live 5 minutes from school. 

Every morning it takes a half hour+ of me coming in his room every couple minutes and telling him to get up, him continuing to lay in the bed and whine, some days getting mad and yelling how he wants to stay home and I “never let him miss even one day!” He has an alarm clock that goes off at 7am and he just shuts it off and goes back to sleep, and then I’m left nagging him the rest of the morning, which is not a great way to start either of our days.

What can I do to help make mornings go more smoothly and get to school on time? I don’t want to be punitive but this can’t continue. I also REALLY don’t want to have to get up earlier but maybe that’s the solution.  What time is their bedtime? Whenever we have late mornings, I can always relate it back to late nights. I also have a 12 year old son and last year we told him that every day I had a wake him up myself, was a day he wouldn’t get any screens. We only allow certain days for video games, but he has a 3D printer he likes to fuss with everyday so that reasoning got him up and going everyday.
